title: arngz refuses a screen whose one space com.apple.spaces has not recorded yet, as just after a display attaches, and its fix line names nothing to do
body:
## What

hv, 19 Oct 2026, at a new desk ("zeopit": two VY229HF displays above the built-in), ran Discover… and arngz refused, exit 2:

```text
arngz: the engine refused discover: the order of screen 2F1BFA83-60AB-4E33-9BC4-BE224243E845's spaces could not be read: no list in com.apple.spaces holds exactly this screen's spaces (3215), so their order is not known (request kept at .../arngz.RVlXoG/request.json); fix: fix what the engine names, then run arngz again
```

The engine orders each screen's spaces by finding the one list in com.apple.spaces' `SpacesDisplayConfiguration` that holds exactly the screen's live spaces (`opt/arngz/lib/plan.lua:618`, D22). Just after displays attach, macOS has not yet written that list. This screen had one space, so its order was never in doubt, and the refusal's fix names nothing a person can do. `apply` reads the screens the same way, so an apply at a newly attached desk is refused too.

## Measured

19 Oct 2026, at `4611b1c`, on hv's machine (macOS 27.0.1).

- 04:08:17Z: run 22 of hv's menuz, `arngz discover --save "$desk" --force`, refused as above. It ran arngz 1.1.0, from menuz's `bin/`.
- 04:12:58Z: `~/Library/Preferences/com.apple.spaces.plist` was last written. Read at 04:17Z through `defaults export`, it holds `[3215]` for `2F1BFA83-...` and `[3212]` for `34791BF3-...`, the two externals' spaces and the newest ids in the domain.
- 04:18:50Z: the same discover, read-only (no `--save`), through the 2.14.0 keg's arngz 1.0.1, whose `order_spaces` is identical: exit 0, with main at 11 spaces and above-left and above-right at 1 each.
- 05:05Z to 05:09Z: hv's Discover… runs 24, 26 and 27 saved zeopit, exit 0.

## Fix

1. A screen with one live space is its own order: `order_spaces` returns it without looking for a list.
2. With two or more live spaces and no list, the refusal says why and what to do: macOS has not recorded this screen's spaces yet, as just after a display attaches, so wait, then run arngz again.
3. `plan_test.lua` pins both: one space and no list is ordered, and two spaces and no list is refused with the new words.
4. `help/arngz.md` and the CHANGELOG's `[2.14.1] - unreleased` say so.

Owner cc, routed by vc on hv's word that everything outstanding ships in 2.14.1 (19 Oct 2026). The design goes here before any source edit, then vc's read, runs booked with the day's booker, vc's read of the bytes, and the landing.

## Design

cc, 19 Oct 2026, with each file:line re-read at main's head `23d7575`, where arngz's files are as they were at `4611b1c`. Size: S.

1. **One space is its own order.** `P.order_spaces` (`opt/arngz/lib/plan.lua:618`) returns `{ id }` for a screen with exactly one live space, before it reads any list. One space has one order, so nothing is guessed, and D22's rule that a screen is never ordered by guess still holds wherever there is an order to know. The comment at `:611` to `:617` says so.
2. **Two or more spaces and no list: the refusal says why and names its fix.** The not-found return (`:639` to `:642`) gains a third value, the fix. The reason becomes `com.apple.spaces has not recorded this screen's spaces (3215, 3216) yet, as just after a display attaches, so their order is not known`, and the fix is `wait for macOS to record them, then run arngz again`. The two-lists refusal (`:633` to `:635`) keeps its words and names no fix, since waiting is not known to clear it. How long macOS takes is not measured: the reads above show only that it had not recorded the list at 04:08:17Z and had by 04:17Z. So the fix names no time, and nothing claims that opening Mission Control hurries it.
3. **The fix travels with the refusal, and the shim does not change.** The shim already prints a fix the engine names (`opt/arngz/arngz:618`), as the engine names one for an apply already running (`opt/arngz/lib/arngz.lua:1412`), and AT-05.3 pins that path (`opt/arngz/test/arngz.bats:895`). On the way there:
   - observe keeps the fix beside the error, as `entry.order_fix` (`arngz.lua:225` to `:229`);
   - `unread` (`plan.lua:232` to `:234`) returns it after its reason, and `P.plan` (`:387` to `:388`) and `P.desk_from_world` (`:1116` to `:1117`) return it third, after `nil` and the refusal;
   - `plan_settled` (`arngz.lua:1054`) and `plan_then` (`:1102`) pass it on, `VERBS.discover` (`:1326`), `VERBS.plan` (`:1334`) and `PHASE.inventory` (`:1119`) hand it to `refuse(why, fix)` (`:43`), and `error_response` (`:1224`) writes it into the response as `fix`.

   Every other refusal names no fix and reads as it does today. `spaces_agree` (`arngz.lua:999`), apply's wait after `create_space` (`:1149`), reads `order_error` as before: a screen that has just gained a space has two or more, so it still waits for the list.

4. **The tests, red first,** in `opt/arngz/test/plan_test.lua`'s space order block (`:519` to `:544`):
   - one space and no list is ordered: `P.order_spaces({ 3215 }, monitors)` gives `{ 3215 }`, hv's screen of 19 Oct;
   - two spaces and no list is refused with the new words and the fix: `P.order_spaces({ 3215, 3216 }, monitors)` gives `nil`, a reason naming `3215` and a display attaching, and a fix naming `run arngz again`;
   - the checks at `:535` (one space, its list second) and `:542` (two lists for one space) are one-space cases, which the change orders before any list is read: `:542` would fail, and `:535` would pass without testing what its name says. Both become two-space cases;
   - the check at `:318` to `:326` (plan refuses an unread order) sets `order_fix` too, and checks that `P.plan` and `P.desk_from_world` return it third.

   On main the two new checks and the extended one fail and the rest pass; with the fix all pass.

5. **Docs.** `help/arngz.md`'s apply bullets gain one after **Displays.** (`:105`): "**A display just attached.** macOS records the order of each display's desktops, and for a display that has just attached it may not have yet. A display with one desktop needs no order. For one with two or more whose order macOS has not recorded yet, arngz refuses, exit 2, and says to wait, then run it again." The CHANGELOG gains a Fixed entry under `[2.14.1] - unreleased`.
6. **Runs,** each booked with gtools-vc: `plan_test.lua` under luajit with the new tests and without the fix, where only the new and extended checks fail; then with the fix, `plan_test.lua` again and `arngz.bats` under bash 3.2 (`/bin` first on PATH) and bash 5. 0077 changes no shell file, so dc's shellcheck run has nothing to check (dc to cc, 05:35Z).
7. **What no suite runs.** The engine's lines in `arngz.lua` load only inside Hammerspoon, and no suite drives a refusal through them, so vc reads them in the bytes. A just-attached display cannot be had on demand, so the hand check is hv's next attach, if hv wants one.
8. **The number is hv's:** arngz 1.1.1 is proposed, a fix on 0070's unreleased 1.1.0, as menuz went from 0.2.0 to 0.3.0 inside this section.
